where: the eleven roster rows in the 'Signed-in team' card — specifically the distance between the name at x=272 and the Active toggle at x=888–958
finding: The admin's actual task on this screen — 'switch off the counselor who left in June' — is now a click 626px to the right of the name that identifies the person, and nothing on the row binds the two together while the pointer travels. Round 1 bought the density (all eleven fit) by pulling the row apart horizontally, but it did not add the pointer affordance that a wide row needs: there is no row hover. If the click lands one row high, Marcus Webb's revocation switches off Miriam Achebe, a core-team member, and the only thing that would tell you is the red Suspended badge that appears 616px to the left of where the cursor is looking. On a page whose subject is adult access to a roster of minors, a silently mis-targeted toggle is the wrong-data failure, not a cosmetic one.
evidence: Row pitch is 53px (dividers measured at y=212, 272, 325, 378 … 802). The Active label pill is min-h-9 = 36px tall on a fine pointer, so there are only 17px of vertical dead zone between one person's toggle and the next person's; a click 27px off-centre is on the wrong human. The only row boundary is a 1px rule in ink-800 (#1e293b) on ink-900 (#0f172a) — 1.18:1, effectively invisible at a glance in the render. The `<li>` carries no hover class at all; the only hover in the row is `@2xl:hover:bg-ink-950` on the 120px role select, which firms up the control but says nothing about which row it belongs to. The access column also reads the identical word 'Active' on all eleven rows including the suspended one (Marcus Webb: unchecked 20px box, label still 'Active'), so post-click verification depends entirely on a 20px tick, or on the badge 616px away.
direction: Give the row a pointer-only hover band — a full-bleed ink-800/40 wash on `@2xl:hover` — so the whole 712px strip lights up under the cursor and the name, the recency, the role and the toggle are visibly one object. While the band is there, the divider can stay faint. Consider also letting the access cell's word follow its state (Active / Suspended) rather than naming the property, so the confirmation of a revoke happens where the click happened.

where: every roster row on the read-only page; the gap between the email address and the 'Last seen' column
finding: The core member's row spans the full 1120px card but carries ink across only about 45% of it. The identity column is 680px wide holding at most 257px of text, so there is a measured 541px void between the end of an address and the start of its recency, and another 165px of empty card to the right of the role badge. The one question this page exists for — who has never signed in — survives it because the warn badge is coloured and pops out, but reading any single person's three facts is a 950px left-to-right traverse with no hover band and a 1.18:1 divider to hold the eye on the line. Wider was not the point of round 1; all eleven rows already fit.
evidence: Measured on the Ana Beltrán row: ink runs from x=272 to x=428 (name/email), then nothing until x=969 ('Last seen 11 days ago'), then nothing from x=1103 until the Counselor badge at x=1151–1227. Card inner right edge is x=1392. The grid is `minmax(0,1fr) 10.5rem 7.5rem 6.5rem` with the badge cluster spanning the last two columns, so on the 1120px core card the 1fr swells to 680px while the admin card gives it 272px and looks correct.
direction: Stop letting the identity column absorb the surplus on the wide card — cap it (or let the whole four-column block sit at a max width and cluster left) so the read-only table has the same reading distance as the admin one. The freed width is not needed for anything else; leaving it as outer margin is cheaper than leaving it inside the row.

where: the recency column on both pages — 'Last seen 12 minutes ago' … 'Last seen 6 days ago', eleven rows
finding: The column re-states its own label on every row. A leader scanning for the stalest volunteer has to skip a constant 62px of 'Last seen ' eleven times before reaching the token that actually varies, and the varying values therefore never share a left edge. This is the one place the new table still reads like a stack of sentences rather than a column of facts.
evidence: The prefix 'Last seen ' measures roughly 62px at text-xs in a 168px (10.5rem) column, leaving about 106px for the value; the values themselves ('12 minutes ago', '2 months ago') start at x≈620 in the admin view and x≈1031 in the core view rather than at the column start. The one row that breaks the pattern — Hannah Boateng's 'Never signed in' warn badge — sits flush at the column start and is visibly easier to find than any of the ten sentences, which is the argument.
direction: The table has earned a header row: one 'Last seen' label above the column and bare values in it. No horizontal space is recovered (the column is fixed either way) but eleven repetitions of scan noise are, and the badge then reads as a value in a labelled column instead of an exception to a sentence.

where: the role column, x≈745–870; Dana Ruiz's row versus Eli Sandoval's row
finding: Two people on this roster are admins and they are drawn in two different visual languages. Dana's role is a filled brand badge; Eli's — the admin an admin can actually demote — is quiet select text. Since round 1 correctly made the select transparent at rest, the single loudest object in the role column is now the one role on the page that cannot be changed, and an admin glancing down the column to answer 'who else can do what I can do' has to read eleven words rather than spot two marks.
evidence: Dana's cell is the brand-500/15 badge at x≈745–793 plus the note 'Another admin has to change this.' spanning into the access column; Eli's cell is `text-ink-100` select text 'Admin' at x≈755 with a chevron at 855, visually identical to the eight 'Counselor' cells and the two 'Core team' cells. The core page has no such split — every role there is a badge — so the two views also disagree with each other on how a role looks.
direction: Pick one resting appearance for a role and let editability be carried by the chevron and the hover state, not by the typography — either the self row's role reads as plain text like the rest, or every role reads as its badge and the select is the hover/focus skin over it. The second also restores the core page's vocabulary to the admin page.
